diagnostic:
S3 REWORK FOR EXAMINE FINDING E17, GREEN. The oracle scenario "While this Foundry opens its secrets key, a start over confirmed from a tab left open changes nothing" (instance-integration-setup.feature:1375) passes, and the whole us-iis-07 lane reads 30 scenarios (30 passed), 532 steps (532 passed), exit 0. The oracle, its supports, the handoff, the ADR and architecture.md are untouched. The record's file list is the cumulative S3 one; this rework touched two of its entries, both under crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/.

THE DEFECT AND THE FIX. The confirmed POST had one refusal answer for two states: started_over read startable(..) - a bool over UnopenableOffer::offers_start_over - and answered AskAgain for everything that was not StartOver, so a stale tab posting to a Foundry whose key opens again was handed the I-28 cost page with a live discard-everything control, which D8 says is not a page that state shows. The two reasons are now two answers with one owner, the domain value L6 already names.

crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/secrets_key_rotation.rs (Modified). UnopenableOffer gains confirmed_post(self) -> ConfirmedStartOver, a total match over its three states: StartOver -> Applies, RestoreOnlyLiveReplica -> AsksAgain, RestoreOnly -> NotOffered. ConfirmedStartOver is a new three-state domain value with no other constructor, so the only way to hold one is to have asked the offer; an unread replica gate stays RestoreOnly and so answers NotOffered, which withholds the way out over a fact this Foundry does not hold (B6). No state, no I/O and no copy was added: the offer table, its gate and its words are unchanged, which is why the existing offer-table test stays green as written.

crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/secrets_key.rs (Modified). started_over matches confirmed_post(): AsksAgain returns StartOverAnswer::AskAgain (the P8 gate refusal, unchanged), NotOffered returns StartOverAnswer::Unchanged, which answers this Foundry's instance integrations page with nothing written, nothing read again and no notice; Applies falls through to the plan, the write and the gate read again inside the locked transaction, so the store-side LiveReplica outcome still answers AskAgain as the root context requires. The private helper startable(..) -> bool became offered(..) -> UnopenableOffer, the one place the door gathers key mode, gate reading and key file; its two callers read the offer they need from it. Second, StartOverCost::Again, the page a refused write lands on, no longer asks unconditionally: it asks where UnopenableOffer::reads_gate holds, which is exactly the I-26 states the live-replica gate decides. The cost page with its control can now not be drawn in a state that offers no way out, by either path, however the gate reads. Module and variant docs say which answer belongs to which reason.

CRAFT SELF-CHECK. No fact is decided twice: the answer comes from the offer, the offer from UnopenableOffer::of_gate, and no template or handler judges the state again. Nothing was generalised for one caller. Rich domain value, no anemic carrier, no application script deciding for it; after GREEN I found no L1-L4 smell in either file, so no RPP delta followed. No separate refactor commit: the rename and widened return type of the private helper are the same coherent delta as the two-answer split and are not separable from it. No test was added, weakened, skipped or rewritten - acceptance owns every test - and the oracle demonstrates both sides of the new rule through the public port: the E17 scenario observes the refusal (the page answered, nothing read about starting over, the stored key, the Activity, Canzan Labs' Slack connection and the saved Slack app all as they were) and "Starting over makes a secrets key this Foundry opens and leaves the workspace told to set up again" observes the accepted path. No commit was made, as the host directed.

COMMANDS, ALL IN THE LIMA VM THROUGH scripts/test-in-lima.sh, EACH EXIT 0. (1) cargo fmt plus cargo test -p foundry-app --lib integrations::secrets_key_rotation (4 passed, 0 failed) and integrations::handlers::secrets_key (3 passed, 0 failed); the formatted bytes were copied back to the Mac. (2) The recorded lane command source scripts/eip-lanes.sh; eip_warm; eip_lane us-iis-07, re-run in this rework: 30 scenarios (30 passed), 532 steps (532 passed). (3) CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 cargo xtask smoke on the final Mac bytes: "xtask smoke :: all gates green", covering cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --release -D warnings, xtask check-arch (boundary guard PASSED, integrations-seal-fence among its rules) and cargo test --workspace --exclude foundry-acceptance --release, in which crates/foundry-store/tests/iis_instance_store.rs ran 19 tests all ok, a_refused_replacement_and_a_lost_compare_and_set_leave_everything_unchanged included. These are my own runs; they replace neither the delivery's recorded verification nor independent review nor EXAMINE.

typesafe: unavailable. The one open choice was where the two-answer decision lives (a domain method on UnopenableOffer, an inline match in the handler, or a second boolean beside offers_start_over). I built the Jev request and ran the client from a shell command; it exited 3 with TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent from this subagent's environment, and reading the login shell's environment was denied by the permission system, so nothing was transmitted and no judgment was obtained. The choice was then settled locally against the bound authority: L6 names UnopenableOffer::decide the owner of the three I-26 states and D8 gives each door its own answer, so the decision belongs on that value and the handler only translates it.
